newsitem.title: EGYPT: Fund raising $50 million to invest in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Fund raising $50 million to invest in Egypt.

text.p: Investments and Securities Group (ISG), a Cairo-based fund manager, is setting up a $50 million closed-end fund to buy into Egyptian companies, ISG Managing Director Ahmed Foda said on Monday.

The fund, to be called the Sphinx Growth Fund, will invest in private unlisted companies as well as companies listed or about to be listed on the Egyptian stock exchange, including privatised state companies in which the government is seeking one or more strategic investors, he said.
"The Sphinx Growth Fund is the first of its kind in Egypt. It will lead to future public offerings and that's what the country needs in this stage," Foda said.
Arab International Bank and Misr Iran Development Bank have already committed $10 million and $5 million respectively.

ISG will also co-manage the Egyptian portion of the Middle East and North African Partners (MENAP), 75 percent guaranteed by the U.S. government through its Overseas Private Investments Corporation (OPIC).
New York-based Siguler Guff and Company is the manager of MENAP with co-managers in regional countries, including Morocco, Tunisia and the Palestinian self-rule territories.
MENAP, with a targeted capital of $250, has attracted $160 million so far, $15 million of it from the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the World Bank's private-sector arm.
"The two funds will be managed in Egypt by ISG," Foda said. "In order not to have conflict of interest, all investments will be shared by both funds on a pro rata basis.
Sphinx will be promoted in the Gulf and European countries, Foda said. Sphinx and MENAP will start operations in Egypt in November, he added.

Sphinx will only buy minority stakes in private companies with the ultimate aim of listing them on the Egyptian stock exchange, he added. "Other exit strategies are repurchase agreements by company owners or selling the stake to a third party," Foda said.
Sphinx, which has a minimum participation of $250,000, will not invest more than 15 percent of its capital in a single entity and not more than 30 percent in one industry.
ISG, established in 1989, has arranged finance and lending facilities to Egyptian-based projects worth 850 million pounds in 1995.
"With plans in the pipeline, the finance facilities will reach between two and three billion pounds in 1996," Foda said.
